bib.title: One Embedder, Any Task: Instruction-Finetuned Text Embeddings
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2023, pages 1102-1121

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; checklist page not needed.

question: Can one embedding model produce task- and domain-aware text embeddings from a natural-language instruction given with the input, without task-specific finetuning?
hypothesis: Text embeddings of the same input can be adjusted to different downstream applications using task and domain descriptions, without further task- or domain-specific finetuning.
contributions: INSTRUCTOR: embeds text together with a task instruction
State-of-the-art on 70 embedding evaluation tasks (66 unseen)
Analysis of instruction robustness, complexity, model size and domain shift

method.summary: Instruction-finetunes GTR (T5-based dual encoder) with a bidirectional in-batch contrastive loss on MEDI, where every input and target is prefixed by an instruction following 'Represent the (domain) text type for task objective:'. Evaluated on MTEB, Billboard and prompt retrieval.
method.task: general-purpose text embedding (retrieval, STS, classification, clustering, reranking, text evaluation, prompt retrieval)

datasets.name: MEDI
datasets.size: 330 datasets: 300 from Super-NaturalInstructions plus 30 from Sentence Transformers embedding data, KILT, MedMCQA; per-dataset instances downsampled (Table 5, e.g. msmarco 175,000, Super-NI 180,000 in total)
datasets.preprocessing: super-NI pairs built with Sentence-T5 cosine similarity: classification uses same/different label among similar examples; other tasks pick highest s_pos as positive and highest s_neg as hard negative. One hard negative plus in-batch for super-NI; four negatives (hard or in-batch) for the other 30. Large datasets downsampled.

datasets.name: Billboard
datasets.preprocessing: English-to-German dropped because models are English only

models.name: INSTRUCTOR (Large)
models.architecture: single T5 encoder, mean pooling over tokens of x

models.name: GPT-J
models.architecture: decoder LM for in-context learning in prompt retrieval

training.objective: Contrastive: softmax over s(x,y)/gamma with s = cosine of instruction-prefixed embeddings; loss also computed with x and y swapped and added (bidirectional in-batch)
training.batch_size: inferred: maximum that fits memory (not stated as a number); each minibatch drawn from a single dataset

other.negatives: 1 hard negative + in-batch for super-NI; 4 negatives for the other 30 datasets
other.sampling: pick a dataset at random each step, build batch only from it so in-batch negatives share the task

inference.samples: not stated; single run per table cell
inference.prompting: instruction prepended: 'Represent the (domain) text type for task objective:'; asymmetric tasks use separate query and doc instructions

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: classification with frozen embeddings and a trained classifier

metrics.name: Spearman
metrics.definition: STS and summarization vs human judgement

metrics.name: Pearson
metrics.definition: Billboard text evaluation vs human judgement, max cosine over references

eval.protocol: Single run per cell, no seeds or significance test reported. Average over 9 categories (7 MTEB, 1 Billboard, 1 prompt retrieval).

limits: Only four negatives per positive due to computation constraints (Section 7).
Could not apply multitask instruction finetuning to GTR-XXL (4.8B) for lack of compute.
Instruction format is a single unified template; paraphrases tested are within the template (Table 6).
Single runs, no seeds or significance tests; training batch size and GPU count not stated.
Instructions help little for retrieval at 335M (+0.4%) and hurt some retrieval sets (MSMARCO, HotpotQA, NQ, Touche2020 at 335M).
